transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-05-03
Time: 10:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Omar Diaz (Redwood SE), Rachel Ng (CSM) - Alex Carter (Nimbus VP Eng), Priya Singh (Nimbus SRE), Tom Jacobs (Nimbus Data Eng)

Summary (auto): follow up on reliability incident, agree next steps for logs, short-term mitigations, and benchmark plan.

00:00:05 - Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run for ~45 minutes. quick agenda - incident review, what we saw in metrics, short term fixes, and next steps. Priya, do you want to start with what you observed?
00:00:22 - Priya Singh: yeah uh thanks lena. so last thursday around 14:10 UTC we saw a spike in 5xxs, mostly 502/503 and a lot of client timeouts. the first thing I should say is traffic spiked about 3x our normal peak for ~8 minutes, so we hit a few rate limits both at the ingress and at the redwood api tier.
00:00:46 - Alex Carter: to add, our gateway also started returning 429s, and then clients retried immediately which made the upstream burst worse. some of the pods serving the model restarted during the window - we saw OOMKilled on two replicas.
00:01:02 - Omar Diaz: okay that's helpful. were the 5xxs correlated with CPU/RTX usage or more with network egress / kv cache misses?
00:01:12 - Priya Singh: it's mixed. CPU on the model nodes did climb but not flat-out saturated; however KV cache miss rate spiked right after restarts, so cold KV warmup caused latency to increase and pushed more requests over the client timeouts.
00:01:27 - Tom Jacobs: yeah the token lengths were skewed - lots of long seqs in that burst which increased per-request work. also our client SDK had a relatively aggressive retry policy: 3 immediate retries with no jitter.
00:01:40 - Lena Park: that immediate retry pattern is a common amplification vector. Omar, do you want to talk through how redwood's routing and rate limits behave during a burst?
00:01:50 - Omar Diaz: sure. so by default we have per-route rate limits and per-shard concurrency controls. when ingress 429s happen clients can retry and then the runtime will see a sudden queue, that can cause 5xx on overloaded shards. we also have small soft-limits before we fail fast; if pods crash and new pods come up, KV cache warmup means those initial requests are heavier. ideally a client-side backoff with exponential jitter reduces the amplification.
00:02:12 - Priya Singh: is there a way to get better visibility into which shard/pod returned 5xxs? our logging currently shows the 5xx but not the redwood-pod id.
00:02:23 - Omar Diaz: yes - we can enable per-request tracing id in the next diagnostic bundle. we'll include pod hostnames and the shard id. for the short term we can also add extra request headers to correlate logs.
00:02:35 - Alex Carter: can you guys also explain the dedicated capacity option cost/benefit? we don't want to jump to dedicated if it's not necessary.
00:02:44 - Lena Park: absolutely. dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools so you don't compete with other customers; it smooths tail latency and reduces the risk of noisy neighbor. cost-wise it's a commitment but we can provision a small burst pool for handling short spikes; i'll send a pricing delta.
00:02:59 - Priya Singh: the burst pool sounds good. but we also need operational changes now - ingress config, retry policy, maybe client-side throttling.
00:03:09 - Omar Diaz: Agreed. for immediate mitigations I suggest three actions: 1) client-side exponential backoff with jitter, cap retries at 2, 2) tune ingress rate-limiter to allow short bursts (burst window) but fail early with clear 429s and header meta, 3) increase pod readiness probe window to avoid sending traffic to pods that just restarted before KV cache warms.
00:03:30 - Tom Jacobs: on readiness probe - we have it at 1 second currently; bumping to 5s might help. question: will warming caches require additional memory?
00:03:41 - Omar Diaz: KV cache warmup is mostly about compute and some GPU memory footprint for caches; if you warm warm loads gradually it's fine. but yes if you maintain larger KV caches you'll need slightly more memory.
00:03:53 - Priya Singh: we can try gradual warmup. also we'll attach the request token length distribution so you can see those long sequences.
00:04:01 - Lena Park: perfect. i also want to call out rate limits at multiple layers: your gateway/nginx ingress, Redwood per-route limits, and client retries. coordination across all three reduces amplification.
00:04:15 - Alex Carter: any quick wins we can implement today?
00:04:20 - Omar Diaz: yes: implement client-side backoff (code change in SDK), reduce retries to 1-2 with exponential jitter, temporarily increase ingress burst allowance, and enable verbose logging for redwood requests. those are low-friction.
00:04:33 - Rachel Ng: i'll draft a short runbook with those items and circulate.
00:04:38 - Priya Singh: one more question - we saw occasional 5xxs labeled as "model error" in the logs. could that be model out-of-memory or a runtime exception?
00:04:48 - Omar Diaz: model errors can be from OOM or internal runtime issues; we'll need the pod logs to confirm. sometimes mis-attributed errors happen when the runtime kills a worker and the client sees a 5xx.
00:04:59 - Tom Jacobs: is there a recommended retry policy for low-latency use cases?
00:05:05 - Omar Diaz: for low-latency, keep retry count low (1-2), use exponential jitter, and increase client-side timeout slightly so you don't retry prematurely. another approach is to move critical traffic to a dedicated pool so you don't need retries.
00:05:19 - Alex Carter: about monitoring - what metrics should we pull into our dashboard?
00:05:24 - Omar Diaz: per-shard qps, per-shard error rate (5xx), KV cache hit/miss, pod restart count, cpu/gpu utilization, and end-to-end p50/p95 latency. also capture ingress 429/queue-depth.
00:05:36 - Priya Singh: we'll export those. can you provide the metric names and a sample prometheus query?
00:05:42 - Omar Diaz: yes, i'll include a doc with prometheus metrics and sample queries.
00:05:47 - Lena Park: let's talk about a small benchmark to reproduce - we propose a run with 10k requests spread across 10 minutes, with a mix of short and long sequences to simulate production token lengths. Priya/Tom, can you provide a representative request file?
00:06:02 - Tom Jacobs: yes we can. we'll anonymize payloads and share the distribution of token lengths by EOD tomorrow.
00:06:09 - Priya Singh: timeline looks good. also, is there any feature flags on Redwood side we can toggle?
00:06:15 - Omar Diaz: we can enable more aggressive batching or change concurrency limits per-shard, but those affect latency. we can also enable more detailed tracing for the benchmark run.
00:06:26 - Alex Carter: trying to quantify cost - if we do a small dedicated instance for peak windows, how do we price that?
00:06:33 - Lena Park: i'll send a delta. there are two typical approaches: small reserved pool billed monthly or per-minute burst capacity billed at higher rate. i'll include both options in the note.
00:06:44 - Priya Singh: security/compliance note - we need logs to be compatible with our SIEM, SSO tokens must not be exposed. we are SOC2 in process so audit logs matter.
00:06:55 - Rachel Ng: we have a SOC 2 pack and a security whitepaper; lena i'll attach the security deck and a short note on KMS and SAML integration in the follow up.
00:07:05 - Lena Park: great. quick clarification - are you using Redwood Hosted or a private VPC deployment for the POC?
00:07:12 - Tom Jacobs: POC started on hosted, but we may move to a VPC if we need tighter network controls.
00:07:18 - Omar Diaz: from a reliability angle, VPC/private deployment gives you more network isolation and can simplify audit requirements, but it adds ops overhead. dedicated hosted capacity is usually enough to smooth bursts.
00:07:30 - Priya Singh: ok - for now let's try the client/ingress changes first and run the benchmark; if that doesn't reduce incidents we'll look at dedicated or VPC.
00:07:39 - Lena Park: sounds like a plan. i'll capture the next steps.
00:07:44 - Alex Carter: any blockers on us sharing logs? we have to scrub some customer data first.
00:07:49 - Priya Singh: we'll scrub PII and share the headers and traces. should be fine by 5/5.
00:07:56 - Lena Park: thanks. Omar, can you outline the retry/backoff sample you mentioned?
00:08:01 - Omar Diaz: sure - sample: initial timeout 8s, max timeout 30s, retry up to 2 times with exponential backoff (base 2) plus full jitter, jitter cap 1s. we'll send sample code snippets for their sdk and for ingress/nginx config.
00:08:18 - Tom Jacobs: that looks reasonable. also we'll increase readiness probe to 5s and liveness to 10s as test.
00:08:27 - Priya Singh: one more thing - rate limit headers. Can Redwood surface remaining quota in response headers so our gateway can make adaptive decisions?
00:08:36 - Omar Diaz: yes we can. we already set X-Redwood-RateLimit-Remaining and X-Redwood-RateLimit-Reset in the hosted responses; if you're on an older agent they might be missing but we'll ensure it's present for the benchmark.
00:08:50 - Rachel Ng: i'll include that in the runbook.
00:08:54 - Lena Park: ok let's move onto the concrete log bundle we need. Priya, you said you'd gather pod logs and kube-proxy logs. can you include timestamps and the request ids you saw?
00:09:05 - Priya Singh: yes we'll include request ids, timestamps, and the ingress logs. also CPU/GPU snapshots for the window.
00:09:13 - Omar Diaz: perfect. when you upload, we'll correlate with our traces and look for mismatch points.
00:09:19 - Alex Carter: any other items?
00:09:22 - Tom Jacobs: curious - the model variant we used was the quantized 8-bit. could that cause instability?
00:09:29 - Omar Diaz: quantization itself shouldn't cause 5xxs; it can slightly change memory profile. the 5xxs we're seeing look more like resource pressure and cold warmup. we'll validate though.
00:09:40 - Priya Singh: okay great.
00:09:42 - Lena Park: recap of next steps - Priya share logs by 5/5, Tom share token-length distribution, Omar share retry/backoff config and prometheus queries by 5/6, Lena share pricing delta by 5/7, Rachel share runbook today. schedule benchmark week of 5/11. any objections?
00:10:02 - Alex Carter: no objections. thanks team.
00:10:06 - Rachel Ng: thanks everyone, i'll send notes and runbook after the call.
00:10:10 - Lena Park: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with attachments.

[End of transcript]
